messages.author: dae01c57a3c54a3a
messages.subject: Vectorized if_else?
parts:
I'm working on vectorizing my implementation of a hierarchical linear ballistic accumulator model of human response time and accuracy.

My latest .stan file is here: https://gist.github.com/mike-lawrence/5867645

I'm getting errors (line 103) seemingly because my assumption that if_else() can be used in the same vectorized manner as ifelse() in R is faulty. Here's the error:

    no matches for function name="if_else"
        arg 0 type=vector
        arg 1 type=vector
        arg 2 type=vector
    available function signatures for if_else:
    0.  if_else(int, real, real) : real


Is there any workaround? 

I tried (see currently-commented-out line 107) doing things with math (take the product of the "if true" vector by the test vector and add the product of the "if false" vector by 1 minus the test vector), but this throws a similar type error:

 no matches for function name="multiply" arg 0 type=vector arg 1 type=vector available function signatures for multiply: 0. multiply(real, real) : real 1. multiply(vector, real) : vector 2. multiply(row vector, real) : row vector 3. multiply(matrix, real) : matrix 4. multiply(row vector, vector) : real 5. multiply(vector, row vector) : matrix 6. multiply(matrix, vector) : vector 7. multiply(row vector, matrix) : row vector 8. multiply(matrix, matrix) : matrix 9. multiply(real, vector) : vector 10. multiply(real, row vector) : row vector 11. multiply(real, matrix) : matrix
Any suggestions would be greatly appreciated! :O)

Mike 

--
Mike Lawrence
Graduate Student
Department of Psychology & Neuroscience
Dalhousie University

~ Certainty is (possibly) folly ~

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Vectorized if_else?
parts:
On 6/26/13 10:18 AM, Mike Lawrence wrote:
> I'm working on vectorizing my implementation of a hierarchical linear ballistic accumulator model of human response time
> and accuracy.
>
> My latest .stan file is here: https://gist.github.com/mike-lawrence/5867645
>
> I'm getting errors (line 103) seemingly because my assumption that if_else() can be used in the same vectorized manner
> as ifelse() in R is faulty.

The appendix of the manual lists all of the available
function signatures. if_else() is not vectorized yet.

We'll eventually get around to vectorizing everything.

Here's the error:
>
> no matches for function name="if_else"
> arg 0 type=vector
> arg 1 type=vector
> arg 2 type=vector
> available function signatures for if_else:
> 0. if_else(int, real, real) : real
>
>
> Is there any workaround?

Just declare a variable to hold the result and assign in a loop.

Assuming t and f are vectors and c a vector you want to test
for zero, then

...if_else(c,t,f)...


{
vector[size(c)] y;
for (i in 1:size(c))
y[x] = if_else(c[i] == 0, t[i], f[i]);

...y...
}

This declares y as a local variable in whatever loop you need it.

It'd be more efficient rather than to define t and f to just
build up y in a loop using the conditional if { ... } else { ... }.
You don't want to create variables you don't use, as it's extra
overhead for auto-diff.

- Bob

    vector a[2];

    a[1] <- 1;
    a[2] <- 2;
    b[1] <- 3;

messages.author: 6ad178c9bfa534b7
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Vectorized if_else?
parts: You can use the elementwise multiplication operator .*

vector[2] a;
    vector[2] b;
    vector[2] c;
    a[1] <- 1;
    a[2] <- 2;
    b[1] <- 3;
    b[2] <- 4;

c <- a .* b;

---
